value: A 0.406 m × 0.94 m SIBAL textile sheet (area density 18 mg/cm²) was ignited at the upstream edge inside the Cygnus flow duct.
Under 20 cm/s concurrent forced airflow, the flame established a steady propagation front rather than blowing off or quenching.
Total burn duration across the large sample sheet lasted approximately 420 s, with an average concurrent flame spread rate of 1.8 mm/s.

activeValue: Sample geometry: 40.6 cm wide × 94 cm long flat panel (0.37 mm thickness, 18 mg/cm² area density)

Source-supported test point for SAFFIRE-I Sample I-1 (concurrent flow): 20 cm/s airflow, 21% O₂ (21.7 to 21.5% O₂ across burn in NTRS 20180005168 Table 1, Slide 30; 21% O₂ and 100 kPa in NTRS 20210011521 Table 2, p. 8), microgravity flame spread rate 1.8 mm/s, burn duration 420 s (~84 cm burn length), steady-state pyrolysis length 4 cm (6.2 cm peak overshoot), and estimated average flame power 1200 ± 300 W (NTRS 20180005168 Slide 25 & Table 1 Slide 31). Companion opposed-flow Sample I-2 burned ~10 cm over 70 s at 1.3 mm/s. Spread rate uncertainty (±) was not reported in Table 1 and remains null.

measurements.explanation: Concurrent flame spread rate of 1.8 mm/s and total burn duration of 420 s for Sample I-1 (0.406 m × 0.94 m SIBAL at 20 cm/s) are directly reported in NTRS 20180005168 Slide 25 and Table 1 (Slide 31). Spread-rate uncertainty is not reported in Table 1 and remains null. (An earlier pre-audit claim of 1.85 ± 0.15 mm/s and 480 s was contradicted by Table 1 and replaced.)

findings.value: Demonstrated that large-scale thin cellulosic fabric (SIBAL) sustains steady concurrent flame spread at ~1.8 mm/s under ISS-like air composition (~21.7% O₂, ~101 kPa) when supplied with 20 cm/s forced ventilation.
findings.source: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20180005168 (Urban et al., 2017, Slides 14, 16, 25, 30–31, Table 1) & https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011521 (ICES-2021-266, p. 8, Table 2)
findings.originalValue: Demonstrated that large-scale thin cellulosic fabric (SIBAL) sustains steady concurrent flame spread at ~1.8 mm/s under ISS-like air composition (~21.7% O₂, ~101 kPa) when supplied with 20 cm/s forced ventilation.
findings.activeValue: In SAFFIRE-I Sample I-1 (40.6 cm × 94 cm × 0.37 mm SIBAL fabric at 20 cm/s concurrent flow, ~21% O₂, 100 kPa), the flame achieved a steady-state spread rate of 1.8 mm/s and a steady pyrolysis length of 4 cm (after an initial ~30% entrance boundary-layer overshoot to 6.2 cm) over a 420 s burn (~84 cm burn length), contrasting with normal-gravity upward burns which accelerated continuously (NTRS 20180005168 Slide 25, Table 1 Slides 30–31; NTRS 20210011521 Table 2 p. 8).

findings.activeValue: On the SAFFIRE-II 9-sample card (Samples II-5 and II-6, 5 cm × 29 cm SIBAL strips), concurrent flame spread propagated completely across the 29 cm strips at 2.1 mm/s (145 s duration at 20 cm/s flow) and 2.6 mm/s (115 s duration at 25 cm/s flow) without exhibiting the 30% entrance flame-length overshoot seen on the wider SAFFIRE-I/III panels because the samples were positioned further downstream in a developed boundary layer (NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 Slides 30–31; NTRS 20210011521 Section III.C p. 8).

value: Thin cast PMMA sample (1.0 mm thickness) sustained ignition and steady concurrent flame propagation under 20 cm/s forced flow at 21.0% O₂ and 101.3 kPa.
Measured flame spread rate across the PMMA slab was 0.35 mm/s, roughly one-fifth the speed of thin SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric under identical airflow.
originalValue: Thin cast PMMA sample (1.0 mm thickness) sustained ignition and steady concurrent flame propagation under 20 cm/s forced flow at 21.0% O₂ and 101.3 kPa.
Measured flame spread rate across the PMMA slab was 0.35 mm/s, roughly one-fifth the speed of thin SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric under identical airflow.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 5 cm wide × 29 cm long two-sided thick slabs (10 mm [1 cm] thickness for flat Sample II-9; structured/grooved surface for Sample II-8)

Source-supported parameters from NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 (Slides 30–31) and NTRS 20210011521 Section III.D (p. 8): Samples II-8 (grooved PMMA, 22.1 to 22.0% O₂, 600 s burn duration) and II-9 (flat 1 cm thick PMMA, 22.0 to 21.9% O₂, 900 s burn duration) were ignited at 97 W for 30 s in 20 cm/s concurrent flow. Both burned ~10 cm in microgravity, reaching limiting flame lengths of 8.0 cm (grooved II-8) and 9.5 cm (flat II-9) while advancing primarily via leading-edge surface regression rather than continuous concurrent spread. Previously claimed 1.0 mm thin-sheet thickness, 0.42 mm/s spread rate, 17.8% LOI, and 310 s duration were contradicted/unverified and removed.
observations.explanation: Earlier pre-audit claims of 1.0 mm thickness, 0.42 mm/s spread rate, and 310 s burn duration were contradicted by NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 (Slides 30–31) and NTRS 20210011521 (p. 8), which report 1 cm (10 mm) flat Sample II-9 burning 900 s (~10 cm burn length, 8.0 cm steady flame length) and grooved Sample II-8 burning 600 s (~10 cm burn length, 9.5 cm steady flame length). Updated active observations and measurementNotes.

findings.value: Thermally thicker polymeric PMMA burns significantly more slowly (~0.35 mm/s) than thin cellulosic fabric (1.69–1.8 mm/s) under identical 20 cm/s normobaric airflow, while still sustaining propagation.
findings.source: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20180005168 (Urban et al., 2017, Slides 14, 30–31, Table 1) & https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011521 (ICES-2021-266, Section III.D, p. 8)
findings.originalValue: Thermally thicker polymeric PMMA burns significantly more slowly (~0.35 mm/s) than thin cellulosic fabric (1.69–1.8 mm/s) under identical 20 cm/s normobaric airflow, while still sustaining propagation.
findings.activeValue: In SAFFIRE-II Samples II-8 (grooved) and II-9 (flat 1 cm thick), two-sided thick PMMA slabs (5 cm × 29 cm) burning in 20 cm/s concurrent flow (~22.0% O₂) remained anchored near the leading edge, advancing via solid surface regression over ~10 cm burn lengths (600 s and 900 s burn durations) and reaching steady limiting flame lengths of 8.0 cm (grooved) and 9.5 cm (flat), whereas 1g comparison tests exhibited acceleratory complete burns (NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 Slides 30–31; NTRS 20210011521 Section III.D p. 8).
findings.explanation: Verified against primary NASA source (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20180005168 (Urban et al., 2017, Slides 14, 30–31, Table 1) & https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011521 (ICES-2021-266, Section III.D, p. 8)). Active value reflects source-supported documentation.

activeValue: Sample geometry: 5 cm wide × 29 cm long strips (Sample II-7: 0.37 mm × 24 cm Nomex with 0.85 mm × 5 cm PMMA starter; Samples II-1..II-4: 0.27, 0.61, 1.03, and 0.37 mm Silicone)

Source-supported results from NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 (Slides 30–31): In Sample II-7 (20 cm/s concurrent flow, ~22.1% O₂, 80 W igniter for 9.2 s), the 5 cm PMMA starter burned for 140 s (5 cm burn length), but the adjacent 24 cm Nomex fabric (0.37 mm thick) exhibited 0 cm burn length and no sustained flame spread (0.0 mm/s). Similarly, all four Silicone strips (II-1 to II-4, thicknesses 0.27–1.03 mm at 20 cm/s, ~22.1% O₂) exhibited 'Insignificant' burn duration and ~0 cm microgravity burn length (whereas 1g comparison strips burned completely or 7.6 cm for II-1, II-2, II-4). Previously claimed 0.8 mm thickness, 3.2 s burn duration, and 22.5% MOC were contradicted/unverified and removed.

findings.originalValue: Raising concurrent forced airflow from 20 cm/s to 30 cm/s in large-scale microgravity testing increased SIBAL flame spread rate by roughly 30% (1.8 mm/s to 2.35 mm/s).
findings.activeValue: Increasing concurrent forced airflow from 20 cm/s (SAFFIRE-I Sample I-1) to 25 cm/s (SAFFIRE-III Sample III-1) over an identical 40.6 cm × 94 cm SIBAL panel (~21% O₂, 100 kPa) increased the steady concurrent flame spread rate proportionally from 1.8 mm/s to 2.3 mm/s (and steady flame length from 4 cm to 5 cm, with an 8.2 cm entrance overshoot), reducing total burn duration from 420 s to 300 s (NTRS 20180005168 Slides 16, 30–31; NTRS 20210011521 Table 2 p. 8).
findings.explanation: Updated finding to state the verified 25 cm/s airflow, 2.3 mm/s concurrent spread rate, and 300 s burn duration (replacing pre-audit 30 cm/s and 2.24 mm/s).

activeValue: Sample geometry: 200 mm long × 400 mm wide structured cast PMMA slab (10 mm base thickness with ten 3 mm-high ribs of 1–10 mm width on both sides; 16 mm total thickness)

Source-supported test conditions for SAFFIRE-V Sample V-4 (structured PMMA in opposed flow): NTRS 20210017838 (Eigenbrod et al., ICES-2021-218, Abstract & Slide 3) reports inflow conditions of 26.9 vol% O₂, 761 hPa (76.1 kPa), 20 cm/s opposed flow for 360 s followed by 5 cm/s for 300 s (660 s total forced-flow duration), and opposed flame spread rate up to 0.88 mm/s along the 1 mm wide rib. Companion overview paper NTRS 20210011521 (Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Table 1, p. 3) lists SAFFIRE-V Sample V-4 at 25.7 mol% O₂ and 72.6 kPa, Sample V-2 (Cotton Jersey, 41 × 50 cm, concurrent) at 26.2 mol% O₂ and 70.7 kPa, and Sample V-3 (1-sided flat 5 mm PMMA, 40 × 18 cm, concurrent) at 25.4 mol% O₂ and 71.3 kPa. Note: The 34% O₂ / 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) atmosphere previously attached to this record was a NASA pre-flight exploration planning boundary (NTRS 20170000230, p. 7), NOT an actual SAFFIRE-V flight test condition; previously claimed 2.65 ± 0.22 mm/s spread rate, 420 s duration, and 15.2% LOI were contradicted/unverified and removed.

findings.value: Despite reduced total pressure (56.5 kPa), 34% O₂ enrichment creates a highly reactive fire environment with rapid ignition, intense radiative heating, and measurable far-field smoke and CO₂ dispersion across the spacecraft cabin.
findings.source: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210017838 (Eigenbrod et al., ICES-2021-218, Abstract & Slides 3–11) & https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011521 (Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Table 1 p. 3 & Section III pp. 4–10)
findings.originalValue: Despite reduced total pressure (56.5 kPa), 34% O₂ enrichment creates a highly reactive fire environment with rapid ignition, intense radiative heating, and measurable far-field smoke and CO₂ dispersion across the spacecraft cabin.
findings.activeValue: In SAFFIRE-V Sample V-4 (200 × 400 mm structured PMMA with 3 mm-high ribs of 1–10 mm width, tested at 26.9 vol% O₂ / 761 hPa [76.1 kPa] in NTRS 20210017838; 25.7 mol% O₂ / 72.6 kPa in NTRS 20210011521 Table 1), initial ignition after preheating produced a rapid (<100 ms) stratified-vapor deflagration, followed by opposed-flow flame spread along the ribs at up to 0.88 mm/s on the 1 mm rib (decreasing with rib width), oxygen-shadowing extinction of downstream flames, and rapid extinction when airflow was shut off after 300 s of 5 cm/s convective cooling (NTRS 20210017838 Abstract & Slides 3, 11; NTRS 20210011521 pp. 3–11).

engineeringInterpretation.value: Exploration atmospheres with ~34% O₂ at ~56.5 kPa represent a substantially higher flammability and thermal hazard than 21% O₂ ISS air, requiring dedicated material screening and post-fire scrubbing evaluation.
engineeringInterpretation.source: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210017838 (Eigenbrod et al., ICES-2021-218, Abstract & Slides 3–11) & https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011521 (Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Table 1 p. 3 & Section III pp. 4–10)
engineeringInterpretation.originalValue: Exploration atmospheres with ~34% O₂ at ~56.5 kPa represent a substantially higher flammability and thermal hazard than 21% O₂ ISS air, requiring dedicated material screening and post-fire scrubbing evaluation.
engineeringInterpretation.activeValue: Thin surface ribs and edges on an otherwise thick (10 mm base) PMMA component act as thermally thin flame-spread pathways in microgravity opposed flow, and flow perturbations or preheating in low-flow zones can create stratified fuel-vapor mixtures that ignite via rapid deflagration. Conversely, stepping airflow down to 5 cm/s to cool the solid before fan shutoff prevented the delayed vapor-jet reignition observed when flow was cut abruptly in SAFFIRE-IV.

value: Thin SIBAL strips (2.2 cm width) were burned in the MSG 7.6 cm × 7.6 cm duct across vitiated nitrogen/oxygen mixtures (16–21% O₂) and low flow velocities (1–35 cm/s).
Flame spread rate decreased monotonically with falling airflow until hitting a low-velocity radiative quenching limit.
Minimum Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) in microgravity forced flow dropped near 16.5% O₂, lower than Earth normal-gravity upward extinction thresholds under gentle forced flow.
observations.source: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20150008962 (Zhao, T'ien, Ferkul, Olson, 2015, pp. 1–9, Appendix Table) & https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011385 (NASA/TM-20210011385, Section 7.0, pp. 93–101 & Appendix A.6, pp. 112–114)
originalValue: Thin SIBAL strips (2.2 cm width) were burned in the MSG 7.6 cm × 7.6 cm duct across vitiated nitrogen/oxygen mixtures (16–21% O₂) and low flow velocities (1–35 cm/s).
Flame spread rate decreased monotonically with falling airflow until hitting a low-velocity radiative quenching limit.
Minimum Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) in microgravity forced flow dropped near 16.5% O₂, lower than Earth normal-gravity upward extinction thresholds under gentle forced flow.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 2.2 cm and 1.2 cm wide × 10 cm exposed length flat strips (0.32 mm thickness, 18.2 mg/cm² area density) in 7.6 cm × 7.6 cm × 17 cm flow duct

Source-supported baseline test conditions from NTRS 20150008962 (Zhao, T'ien, Ferkul, Olson, 2015, Section 2–3, pp. 2–4, Figure 2 & Appendix Test GMT96-T7, p. 9; also NASA/TM-20210011385 Section 7.0, pp. 93–101): 2.2 cm × 10 cm SIBAL strip at 10 cm/s concurrent flow, 21% O₂, 1 atm (101.3 kPa), reaching a limiting constant length at ~19 s with steady spread for ~9 s and total burn duration of ~40 s (and >60 s at 5 cm/s in Test GMT96-T8, Fig. 3). Across 27 BASS-II tests (16.4–21.0% O₂, 1–53 cm/s), low-speed quenching velocities were measured between 1 and 5 cm/s (e.g., quenching at 2.2 cm/s in 18.7% O₂ in Test GMT45-T4, Figs. 5–6). Because steady spread rates are plotted graphically in Figure 4 (p. 5) without a numeric table for the previously claimed 1.45 ± 0.11 mm/s and 16.2 ± 0.4% LOI, those unverified point values remain null.

measurements.explanation: In NTRS 20150008962, flame spread rates vs. flow velocity are plotted graphically in Figure 4 (p. 5) without a numeric table confirming the earlier pre-audit claim of 1.45 ± 0.11 mm/s, and Section 3 (p. 7) states the minimum-oxygen boundary could not be accurately determined by the velocity-stepping procedure (lowest tested was 16.4% O₂, not 16.2 ± 0.4% O₂). All numerical measurement values and uncertainties are quarantined to null, with ~40 s baseline burn time (p. 3) noted in measurementNotes.

findings.value: In microgravity low-speed forced flow (1–15 cm/s), thin cellulosic fabric exhibits both a low-flow radiative quenching boundary (near 1–3 cm/s) and a lower Limiting Oxygen Index (~16.5% O₂) than standard Earth natural-convection benchmarks.
findings.source: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20150008962 (Zhao, T'ien, Ferkul, Olson, 2015, pp. 1–9, Appendix Table) & https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011385 (NASA/TM-20210011385, Section 7.0, pp. 93–101 & Appendix A.6, pp. 112–114)
findings.originalValue: In microgravity low-speed forced flow (1–15 cm/s), thin cellulosic fabric exhibits both a low-flow radiative quenching boundary (near 1–3 cm/s) and a lower Limiting Oxygen Index (~16.5% O₂) than standard Earth natural-convection benchmarks.
findings.activeValue: Across 27 BASS-II and 4 BASS concurrent-flow tests on 1.2 cm and 2.2 cm wide × 10 cm long SIBAL fabric strips in the ISS MSG duct (16.4–21% O₂, 1 atm, 1–53 cm/s), flames at 5–10 cm/s (21% O₂) reached steady limiting lengths and spread rates (~40 s total burn at 10 cm/s; >60 s at 5 cm/s), while stepping flow velocity down revealed a radiative/conductive low-speed quenching boundary between 1 and 5 cm/s where flames shrank into dim blue circular shapes before extinguishing (NTRS 20150008962 pp. 1–9; NTRS 20210011385 Section 7.0 pp. 93–101).

engineeringInterpretation.value: Quiescent or zero-flow regions promote radiative self-extinguishment, whereas gentle cabin ventilation (5–15 cm/s) stabilizes flame spread even in slightly oxygen-vitiated atmospheres.
engineeringInterpretation.source: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20150008962 (Zhao, T'ien, Ferkul, Olson, 2015, pp. 1–9, Appendix Table) & https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011385 (NASA/TM-20210011385, Section 7.0, pp. 93–101 & Appendix A.6, pp. 112–114)
engineeringInterpretation.originalValue: Quiescent or zero-flow regions promote radiative self-extinguishment, whereas gentle cabin ventilation (5–15 cm/s) stabilizes flame spread even in slightly oxygen-vitiated atmospheres.
engineeringInterpretation.activeValue: Microgravity eliminates buoyant natural convection (which is ~20–30 cm/s in 1g), exposing a low-velocity regime (5–15 cm/s) where thin fabrics sustain steady concurrent spread, bounded below by radiative/conductive quenching at 1–5 cm/s (with higher quenching speeds required at lower O₂ concentrations).

value: Cylindrical cast PMMA rods and flat PMMA samples were ignited in microgravity inside the ISS MSG duct.
Under opposed and concurrent flows between 1.5 and 25 cm/s, steady spread over PMMA rods proceeded at ~0.42 mm/s near 21% O₂ and 10 cm/s.
Extinction occurred when oxygen fell below ~17.5% O₂ or when forced flow dropped below radiative quenching thresholds.
originalValue: Cylindrical cast PMMA rods and flat PMMA samples were ignited in microgravity inside the ISS MSG duct.
Under opposed and concurrent flows between 1.5 and 25 cm/s, steady spread over PMMA rods proceeded at ~0.42 mm/s near 21% O₂ and 10 cm/s.
Extinction occurred when oxygen fell below ~17.5% O₂ or when forced flow dropped below radiative quenching thresholds.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 6.35 mm, 9.52 mm, and 12.7 mm diameter (radii 0.318, 0.476, and 0.635 cm) × 5.9 cm initial length cylindrical rods with hemispherical stagnation tips

Source-supported values from NASA/TM-20210011385 (NTRS 20210011385, Section 6.1, Olson, pp. 64–76): Across tests spanning 13.6–22.2% O₂ and 0–55 cm/s flow on 5.9 cm long PMMA rods (radii 0.318, 0.476, 0.635 cm), the empirical U-shaped flammability boundary (Eq. 6.1, Figs. 6.9–6.10, pp. 75–76) reaches a minimum oxygen concentration of 13.5% O₂ at stretch rate a = 8–12 s⁻¹ (1.9% O₂ lower than the 15.4% O₂ normal-gravity upward limit). In the lowest-O₂ quenching test (r = 0.476 cm rod, initial 14.8% O₂, final 13.6% O₂, flow stepped down to 1.5 cm/s, Figs. 6.4–6.6, pp. 69–72), the rod tip reached a steady-state regression velocity Vr = 0.0385 mm/s and oscillated at 1.1 Hz before quenching. Because this record spans a multi-test flammability boundary with quench tests lasting up to 28 min (p. 69), single-point ambient conditions and burn duration are left null; previously claimed 100 mm length, 0.18 ± 0.03 mm/s spread rate, 17.4% LOI, and 95 s duration were contradicted/unverified and removed.
observations.explanation: Earlier pre-audit claims (100 mm rod length, 0.18 mm/s spread rate, 17.4% O₂ LOI, 95 s burn duration) were contradicted by NASA/TM-20210011385 Section 6.1, which reports initial rod length Lo = 5.9 cm (p. 64), three radii (0.318, 0.476, 0.635 cm, p. 67), steady rod tip regression rate Vr = 0.0385 mm/s at 13.6% O₂ quenching (p. 69), and a U-shaped flammability boundary minimum of 13.5% O₂ at stretch rate a = 8–12 s⁻¹ vs. 15.4% O₂ in 1g upward burning (pp. 75–76). Updated active record.

findings.value: Cast PMMA exhibits slower flame spread (~0.42 mm/s) and a slightly higher LOI (~17.5% O₂) than thin SIBAL fabric in microgravity low-speed flows, with extinction governed by surface radiative heat losses at very low velocities.
findings.source: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011385 (NASA/TM-20210011385, Olson et al., Section 6.1, pp. 64–92 & Appendix A.5, pp. 110–111)
findings.originalValue: Cast PMMA exhibits slower flame spread (~0.42 mm/s) and a slightly higher LOI (~17.5% O₂) than thin SIBAL fabric in microgravity low-speed flows, with extinction governed by surface radiative heat losses at very low velocities.
findings.activeValue: In BASS-II axial stagnation-flow tests on cast PMMA rods (radii 0.318–0.635 cm, initial length 5.9 cm) across 13.6–22.2% O₂ and 0–55 cm/s flow, sustained ignition required ≥14.5% O₂ (with ignition delays up to 230 s near the limit), but pre-warmed burning rods survived down to 13.6% O₂ (with steady rod tip regression of 0.0385 mm/s and 1.1 Hz flame oscillations prior to radiative quenching), defining a U-shaped flammability boundary with a minimum of 13.5% O₂ at low stretch rates (8–12 s⁻¹) compared to 15.4% O₂ in 1g upward screening (NTRS 20210011385 Section 6.1, pp. 64–76).

engineeringInterpretation.value: Reducing forced ventilation below critical quenching speeds suppresses thick polymer flames in microgravity, whereas persistent 10–15 cm/s ventilation sustains slow but steady burning.
engineeringInterpretation.source: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210011385 (NASA/TM-20210011385, Olson et al., Section 6.1, pp. 64–92 & Appendix A.5, pp. 110–111)
engineeringInterpretation.originalValue: Reducing forced ventilation below critical quenching speeds suppresses thick polymer flames in microgravity, whereas persistent 10–15 cm/s ventilation sustains slow but steady burning.
engineeringInterpretation.activeValue: PMMA rods in microgravity remain flammable in a low-velocity 'Goldilocks' ventilation zone (~1–5 cm/s) down to 13.5% O₂—1.9% O₂ lower than normal-gravity upward screening (15.4% O₂)—and require up to 230 s to ignite near the limit, showing that NASA-STD-6001 Test 1's 25 s normal-gravity ignition protocol is non-conservative for preheated thick polymers in low-speed spacecraft ventilation.

value: Large isolated n-heptane droplets (2.5–4.5 mm initial diameter) formed spherical diffusion flames in quiescent microgravity inside the ISS CIR.
Unlike small droplets that burn out completely, larger heptane droplets experienced radiative extinction of the hot visible flame while droplet fuel remained.
Following visible hot-flame extinction, n-heptane droplets continued vaporizing under non-visible low-temperature cool-flame combustion producing partial oxidation products.

originalValue: Large isolated n-heptane droplets (2.5–4.5 mm initial diameter) formed spherical diffusion flames in quiescent microgravity inside the ISS CIR.
Unlike small droplets that burn out completely, larger heptane droplets experienced radiative extinction of the hot visible flame while droplet fuel remained.
Following visible hot-flame extinction, n-heptane droplets continued vaporizing under non-visible low-temperature cool-flame combustion producing partial oxidation products.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 2–5 mm initial diameter free-floating and 80-µm fiber-supported spherical droplets (Test FLEX-008: 2.95 mm ± 0.05 mm initial diameter free-floating n-heptane droplet)

Source-supported test point for FLEX-008 (identifier 30CAL06, April 10, 2009) from NASA/TP-2015-216046 (NTRS 20150023456, Table I p. 9 & Table IX p. 20): free-floating n-heptane droplet in ISS cabin air (0.21 O₂ mole fraction, 0.79 N₂, 762.4 mmHg = 101.6 kPa), actual initial diameter D₀ = 2.95 mm (±50 µm [±0.05 mm] HiBMs droplet diameter uncertainty per Section 3.1.2, p. 8), average burning-rate constant K = 0.79 mm²/s, and burn time 14.8 s (companion cabin-air test FLEX-007 with D₀ = 1.87 mm had K = 0.67 mm²/s and burn time 5.3 s). Across the 284-test campaign (0.70–3.05 atm), N₂-diluted heptane tests (Table V, p. 12) were conducted down to 13.4% O₂. Linear flame spread rate (mm/s) is not applicable to spherical droplet regression (mm²/s). Previously claimed 6.8 s burn duration and 13.8 ± 0.5% LOI were contradicted/unverified in NASA/TP-2015-216046 and removed.
observations.explanation: Updated observations to cite exact test FLEX-008 (D₀ = 2.95 mm ± 0.05 mm, 21.0% O₂, 762.4 mmHg = 101.6 kPa, K = 0.79 mm²/s, burn time = 14.8 s) and FLEX-007 (D₀ = 1.87 mm, K = 0.67 mm²/s, burn time = 5.3 s) from Table IX (p. 20), replacing the contradicted pre-audit claim of 6.8 s burn duration and clarifying that NASA/TP-2015-216046 archives the 284 hot-flame droplet tests.

activeValue.measurementNotes: Source-supported test point for FLEX-008 (identifier 30CAL06, April 10, 2009) from NASA/TP-2015-216046 (NTRS 20150023456, Table I p. 9 & Table IX p. 20): free-floating n-heptane droplet in ISS cabin air (0.21 O₂ mole fraction, 0.79 N₂, 762.4 mmHg = 101.6 kPa), actual initial diameter D₀ = 2.95 mm (±50 µm [±0.05 mm] HiBMs droplet diameter uncertainty per Section 3.1.2, p. 8), average burning-rate constant K = 0.79 mm²/s, and burn time 14.8 s (companion cabin-air test FLEX-007 with D₀ = 1.87 mm had K = 0.67 mm²/s and burn time 5.3 s). Across the 284-test campaign (0.70–3.05 atm), N₂-diluted heptane tests (Table V, p. 12) were conducted down to 13.4% O₂. Linear flame spread rate (mm/s) is not applicable to spherical droplet regression (mm²/s). Previously claimed 6.8 s burn duration and 13.8 ± 0.5% LOI were contradicted/unverified in NASA/TP-2015-216046 and removed.

measurements.explanation: Replaced contradicted pre-audit burn duration (6.8 s) and unverified LOI (13.8 ± 0.5% O₂) with the Table IX (p. 20) measurement for test FLEX-008: burnDurationSec = 14.8 s (uncertainty null; flameSpreadRate and LOI null; K = 0.79 mm²/s documented in measurementNotes).

findings.value: Discovered dual-stage combustion in microgravity liquid heptane droplets: visible flames extinguish radiatively below ~15–21% O₂ depending on diluent, yet low-temperature cool flames persist invisibly, generating aldehydes and CO.

findings.originalValue: Discovered dual-stage combustion in microgravity liquid heptane droplets: visible flames extinguish radiatively below ~15–21% O₂ depending on diluent, yet low-temperature cool flames persist invisibly, generating aldehydes and CO.
findings.activeValue: In NASA/TP-2015-216046 (archiving the first 284 FLEX tests on ISS), free-floating n-heptane and methanol droplets (2–5 mm initial diameter) burned with spherical symmetry in quiescent microgravity across 0.70–3.05 atm, exhibiting radiative extinction at larger droplet diameters under high dilution, diffusive extinction at smaller diameters, and disruptive extinction; in cabin air (Test FLEX-008: 21% O₂, 762.4 mmHg [101.6 kPa]), a 2.95 mm n-heptane droplet burned for 14.8 s with an average d²-law burning-rate constant of K = 0.79 mm²/s (NTRS 20150023456, pp. 1, 8–12, 20).

activeValue: Sample geometry: 25 mm and 50 mm diameter circular porous gas-fueled burners with perforated outlet plates and heat-flux sensors

Investigation overview record backed by NTRS 20170009141 (Markan, Quintiere, Sunderland, de Ris, Stocker, 2017, pp. 1–6) and NTRS 20160010073 (Markan et al., 2015, Slides 1–10): ~53 microgravity drop tests (5.18 s free fall) were conducted across 25 mm and 50 mm burner diameters, 21–30% O₂ (0.21–0.30 mole fraction), 0.5–1.0 atm (50.7–101.3 kPa), and 3.5–12.7 g/m²s fuel flux to emulate condensed fuels with heats of gasification L = 0.4–4 kJ/g. In Test 92 (ethylene, 30% O₂, 0.7 atm, NTRS 20160010073 Slide 5), net surface heat flux reached ~3 kW/m² on the 25 mm burner vs. ~7 kW/m² on the 50 mm burner. Single-point conditions and measurements remain null on this overview record; previously cited NTRS 20205008253 returned HTTP 404 and was replaced with verified NTRS 20170009141 and NTRS 20160010073.

findings.value: Investigation overview: BRE provides fundamental flammability boundary maps across 15–35% O₂ and 50–101.3 kPa by matching thermal feedback and gasification parameters of real spacecraft materials.
findings.source: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20170009141 (Markan et al., 2017, pp. 1–6) & https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20160010073 (Markan et al., 2015, Slides 1–10)
findings.originalValue: Investigation overview: BRE provides fundamental flammability boundary maps across 15–35% O₂ and 50–101.3 kPa by matching thermal feedback and gasification parameters of real spacecraft materials.
findings.activeValue: Microgravity Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) tests using 25 mm and 50 mm circular gas burners (methane and ethylene across 21–30% O₂ and 0.5–1.0 atm in quiescent microgravity) produced hemispherical flames whose surface heat flux approached quasi-steady state within ~5 s (while flame height reached only ~37% of steady state in 5 s, motivating long-duration ISS tests), and demonstrated higher net surface heat flux on the 50 mm burner (~7 kW/m² vs. ~3 kW/m² at 30% O₂, 0.7 atm) due to increased gas-phase radiation from the larger flame volume (NTRS 20170009141 pp. 1–6; NTRS 20160010073 Slides 3–6).

activeValue: Sample geometry: Cylindrical cast PMMA rods (12.7 mm diameter × 150–154 mm length) centered in a 70 mm ID quartz flow tube with three equispaced halogen radiant heaters (up to 40 kW/m²) and downstream Kanthal wire pilot

Investigation overview record backed by NTRS 20200000361 (Ferkul et al., 2019, Slides 3–5, 11–16) and NTRS 20150023467 (Fernandez-Pello, 2013, pp. 1–13): MIST apparatus tests 12.7 mm diameter × 154 mm length cast PMMA rods (22 rod samples of 15 cm nominal length allocated in SoFIE CIR insert, NTRS 20200000361 Slide 11) under external radiant flux up to 40 kW/m², 14–30% O₂, and 10–100 cm/s flow. Direct numerical simulations in NTRS 20150023467 (Section Modeling Task, pp. 8–10, Figs. 12–13) at 100 kPa, 21% O₂, 40 cm/s (0.4 m/s) flow, and 16 kW/m² radiant flux predicted piloted ignition at 596 s in 0g vs. 774 s in 1g. Single-point flight measurements remain null on this overview record; previously cited NTRS 20220014842 was an unrelated aircraft human-autonomy paper and was replaced with verified NTRS 20200000361 and NTRS 20150023467.

findings.value: Investigation overview: SoFIE-MIST targets thermally-assisted solid-fuel ignition and suppression limits under exploration-relevant oxygen/pressure combinations aboard the ISS.
findings.originalValue: Investigation overview: SoFIE-MIST targets thermally-assisted solid-fuel ignition and suppression limits under exploration-relevant oxygen/pressure combinations aboard the ISS.
findings.activeValue: The SoFIE-MIST investigation and apparatus (12.7 mm × 150–154 mm cast PMMA rods irradiated by three halogen heaters up to 40 kW/m² across 14–30% O₂ and 10–100 cm/s flow) demonstrated an exponential decay in ignition delay time with increasing incident radiant heat flux, an approximately constant critical mass loss rate at ignition across heat fluxes, statistically significant differences between virgin and re-ignited PMMA samples, and earlier predicted piloted ignition in microgravity than normal gravity (596 s in 0g vs. 774 s in 1g at 16 kW/m², 21% O₂, 100 kPa, 40 cm/s in FDS-DNS modeling) due to absence of buoyant Rayleigh-Taylor cooling instabilities (NTRS 20200000361 Slides 4, 11; NTRS 20150023467 pp. 2–10).

summary.value: Conducted realistic spacecraft combustion and far-field smoke/gas diagnostics under an exploration-class reduced-pressure, elevated-oxygen atmosphere (56.5 kPa, 34% O₂) after Cygnus unberthing.
summary.originalValue: Conducted realistic spacecraft combustion and far-field smoke/gas diagnostics under an exploration-class reduced-pressure, elevated-oxygen atmosphere (56.5 kPa, 34% O₂) after Cygnus unberthing.
summary.activeValue: Conducted large-scale spacecraft fire growth, extinction, and far-field smoke/gas transport experiments inside Cygnus (NG-14, January 2021) at reduced pressure and elevated oxygen (reported as 25.4–26.2 mol% O₂ and 70.7–72.6 kPa across Samples V-2, V-3, and V-4 in NTRS 20210011521 Table 1, and 26.9 vol% O₂ at 761 hPa [76.1 kPa] for structured PMMA Sample V-4 in NTRS 20210017838). Note: 34% O₂ / 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) is a NASA exploration atmosphere planning reference (NTRS 20170000230), not an established SAFFIRE-V flight test condition.
summary.explanation: Original summary claimed SAFFIRE-V ran at '56.5 kPa, 34% O₂'. Primary post-flight SAFFIRE-V papers contradict this: NTRS 20210011521 Table 1 (p. 3) reports 25.4–26.2 mol% O₂ and 70.7–72.6 kPa across Samples V-2, V-3, and V-4, and NTRS 20210017838 (Abstract & Slide 3) reports 26.9 vol% O₂ and 761 hPa (76.1 kPa) for structured PMMA Sample V-4. The 34% O₂ / 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) setting was a pre-flight planning boundary (NTRS 20170000230, p. 7). Updated active summary.

originalValue: A 0.406 m × 0.94 m SIBAL textile sheet (area density 18 mg/cm²) was ignited at the upstream edge inside the Cygnus flow duct.
Under 20 cm/s concurrent forced airflow, the flame established a steady propagation front rather than blowing off or quenching.
Total burn duration across the large sample sheet lasted approximately 420 s, with an average concurrent flame spread rate of 1.8 mm/s.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 40.6 cm wide × 94 cm long flat panel (0.37 mm thickness, 18 mg/cm² area density)

Source-supported test point for SAFFIRE-I Sample I-1 (concurrent flow): 20 cm/s airflow, 21% O₂ (21.7 to 21.5% O₂ across burn in NTRS 20180005168 Table 1, Slide 30; 21% O₂ and 100 kPa in NTRS 20210011521 Table 2, p. 8), microgravity flame spread rate 1.8 mm/s, burn duration 420 s (~84 cm burn length), steady-state pyrolysis length 4 cm (6.2 cm peak overshoot), and estimated average flame power 1200 ± 300 W (NTRS 20180005168 Slide 25 & Table 1 Slide 31). Companion opposed-flow Sample I-2 burned ~10 cm over 70 s at 1.3 mm/s. Spread rate uncertainty (±) was not reported in Table 1 and remains null.

records.originalValue: Demonstrated that large-scale thin cellulosic fabric (SIBAL) sustains steady concurrent flame spread at ~1.8 mm/s under ISS-like air composition (~21.7% O₂, ~101 kPa) when supplied with 20 cm/s forced ventilation.
records.activeValue: In SAFFIRE-I Sample I-1 (40.6 cm × 94 cm × 0.37 mm SIBAL fabric at 20 cm/s concurrent flow, ~21% O₂, 100 kPa), the flame achieved a steady-state spread rate of 1.8 mm/s and a steady pyrolysis length of 4 cm (after an initial ~30% entrance boundary-layer overshoot to 6.2 cm) over a 420 s burn (~84 cm burn length), contrasting with normal-gravity upward burns which accelerated continuously (NTRS 20180005168 Slide 25, Table 1 Slides 30–31; NTRS 20210011521 Table 2 p. 8).

records.activeValue: Large-scale microgravity concurrent flames over thin charring fabrics do not accelerate indefinitely as in 1g buoyant upward spread; instead, flow-duct confinement and boundary-layer development govern a finite limiting flame length and steady spread rate proportional to forced ventilation velocity.

originalValue: A 5 cm × 29 cm SIBAL control strip was burned alongside eight engineering spacecraft materials inside the SAFFIRE-II flow duct.
Under 20 cm/s forced flow at 21.0% O₂ and 101.3 kPa, the narrow SIBAL control sample propagated at 1.69 mm/s.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 5 cm wide × 29 cm long strip (0.37 mm thickness, 18 mg/cm² area density)

Source-supported test point for SAFFIRE-II Sample II-5 (5 cm × 29 cm SIBAL strip at 20 cm/s concurrent flow, 21% O₂ and 100 kPa in NTRS 20210011521 Table 2 p. 8; ~22.1% O₂ in NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 Slide 30): spread rate 2.1 mm/s, burn duration 145 s (29 cm complete burn length), steady flame size 4 cm, and estimated average flame power 200 ± 50 W (NTRS 20180005168 Slide 25 & Table 1 Slide 31). Companion Sample II-6 at 25 cm/s concurrent flow burned 29 cm in 115 s at 2.6 mm/s (steady flame size 5 cm). Previously claimed LOI (18.5% O₂) and spread rate (1.72 ± 0.12 mm/s) were contradicted/unverified and removed.

originalValue: Thin cast PMMA sample (1.0 mm thickness) sustained ignition and steady concurrent flame propagation under 20 cm/s forced flow at 21.0% O₂ and 101.3 kPa.
Measured flame spread rate across the PMMA slab was 0.35 mm/s, roughly one-fifth the speed of thin SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric under identical airflow.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 5 cm wide × 29 cm long two-sided thick slabs (10 mm [1 cm] thickness for flat Sample II-9; structured/grooved surface for Sample II-8)

Source-supported parameters from NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 (Slides 30–31) and NTRS 20210011521 Section III.D (p. 8): Samples II-8 (grooved PMMA, 22.1 to 22.0% O₂, 600 s burn duration) and II-9 (flat 1 cm thick PMMA, 22.0 to 21.9% O₂, 900 s burn duration) were ignited at 97 W for 30 s in 20 cm/s concurrent flow. Both burned ~10 cm in microgravity, reaching limiting flame lengths of 8.0 cm (grooved II-8) and 9.5 cm (flat II-9) while advancing primarily via leading-edge surface regression rather than continuous concurrent spread. Previously claimed 1.0 mm thin-sheet thickness, 0.42 mm/s spread rate, 17.8% LOI, and 310 s duration were contradicted/unverified and removed.
records.explanation: Earlier pre-audit claims of 1.0 mm thickness, 0.42 mm/s spread rate, and 310 s burn duration were contradicted by NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 (Slides 30–31) and NTRS 20210011521 (p. 8), which report 1 cm (10 mm) flat Sample II-9 burning 900 s (~10 cm burn length, 8.0 cm steady flame length) and grooved Sample II-8 burning 600 s (~10 cm burn length, 9.5 cm steady flame length). Updated active observations and measurementNotes.

Both burned ~10 cm in microgravity, reaching limiting flame lengths of 8.0 cm (grooved II-8) and 9.5 cm (flat II-9) while advancing primarily via leading-edge surface regression rather than continuous concurrent spread. Previously claimed 1.0 mm thin-sheet thickness, 0.42 mm/s spread rate, 17.8% LOI, and 310 s duration were contradicted/unverified and removed.

records.explanation: Earlier pre-audit claims (0.42 ± 0.05 mm/s spread rate, 17.8 ± 0.4% LOI, 310 s duration) were contradicted by NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 (Slide 31), which reports 600 s burn duration for Sample II-8 and 900 s for Sample II-9, with flameSpreadRate listed as 'Note (iv)' (anchored leading-edge flame) and no LOI sweep. Updated burnDurationSec to 600 s and kept flameSpreadRate and LOI null.

records.originalValue: Thermally thicker polymeric PMMA burns significantly more slowly (~0.35 mm/s) than thin cellulosic fabric (1.69–1.8 mm/s) under identical 20 cm/s normobaric airflow, while still sustaining propagation.
records.activeValue: In SAFFIRE-II Samples II-8 (grooved) and II-9 (flat 1 cm thick), two-sided thick PMMA slabs (5 cm × 29 cm) burning in 20 cm/s concurrent flow (~22.0% O₂) remained anchored near the leading edge, advancing via solid surface regression over ~10 cm burn lengths (600 s and 900 s burn durations) and reaching steady limiting flame lengths of 8.0 cm (grooved) and 9.5 cm (flat), whereas 1g comparison tests exhibited acceleratory complete burns (NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 Slides 30–31; NTRS 20210011521 Section III.D p. 8).

records.originalValue: Higher fuel thermal inertia and pyrolysis energy of PMMA slow propagation compared to textiles, though sustained burning at 21% O₂ demonstrates that solid thermoplastics remain flammable under moderate cabin ventilation.
records.activeValue: Thick non-charring PMMA slabs in microgravity concurrent flow reach a finite limiting flame length governed by downstream radiative heat loss at the pyrolysis tip and propagate via leading-edge regression rather than rapid concurrent surface spread, demonstrating a fundamental regime difference from 1g upward NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 screening.

originalValue: Nomex HT90-40 aramid fabric strip was exposed to the igniter wire under 20 cm/s airflow at 21.0% O₂ and 101.3 kPa.
Once the external igniter energy was removed, the Nomex sample self-extinguished and did not sustain flame spread.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 5 cm wide × 29 cm long strips (Sample II-7: 0.37 mm × 24 cm Nomex with 0.85 mm × 5 cm PMMA starter; Samples II-1..II-4: 0.27, 0.61, 1.03, and 0.37 mm Silicone)

Source-supported results from NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 (Slides 30–31): In Sample II-7 (20 cm/s concurrent flow, ~22.1% O₂, 80 W igniter for 9.2 s), the 5 cm PMMA starter burned for 140 s (5 cm burn length), but the adjacent 24 cm Nomex fabric (0.37 mm thick) exhibited 0 cm burn length and no sustained flame spread (0.0 mm/s). Similarly, all four Silicone strips (II-1 to II-4, thicknesses 0.27–1.03 mm at 20 cm/s, ~22.1% O₂) exhibited 'Insignificant' burn duration and ~0 cm microgravity burn length (whereas 1g comparison strips burned completely or 7.6 cm for II-1, II-2, II-4). Previously claimed 0.8 mm thickness, 3.2 s burn duration, and 22.5% MOC were contradicted/unverified and removed.

records.originalValue: Raising concurrent forced airflow from 20 cm/s to 30 cm/s in large-scale microgravity testing increased SIBAL flame spread rate by roughly 30% (1.8 mm/s to 2.35 mm/s).
records.activeValue: Increasing concurrent forced airflow from 20 cm/s (SAFFIRE-I Sample I-1) to 25 cm/s (SAFFIRE-III Sample III-1) over an identical 40.6 cm × 94 cm SIBAL panel (~21% O₂, 100 kPa) increased the steady concurrent flame spread rate proportionally from 1.8 mm/s to 2.3 mm/s (and steady flame length from 4 cm to 5 cm, with an 8.2 cm entrance overshoot), reducing total burn duration from 420 s to 300 s (NTRS 20180005168 Slides 16, 30–31; NTRS 20210011521 Table 2 p. 8).
records.explanation: Updated finding to state the verified 25 cm/s airflow, 2.3 mm/s concurrent spread rate, and 300 s burn duration (replacing pre-audit 30 cm/s and 2.24 mm/s).
records.reviewerNotes: Verified against NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 (Slides 30–31).

records.originalValue: Demonstrates positive sensitivity of concurrent microgravity flame spread to cabin ventilation velocity in the 20–30 cm/s regime, underscoring the importance of ventilation shutdown protocols in fire mitigation studies.
records.activeValue: In forced-convection microgravity environments, large-scale concurrent flame spread rate over thin charring fabrics scales nearly linearly with ventilation velocity, meaning cabin HVAC flow reductions directly slow fire propagation.

originalValue: Cygnus cabin atmosphere was conditioned to a reduced-pressure, oxygen-enriched exploration environment (~56.5 kPa / 8.2 psia and ~34% O₂) prior to sequential ignitions.
Elevated oxygen mole fraction produced vigorous, brighter flames and substantially greater radiant heat flux than normobaric 21% O₂ tests.
Far-field diagnostic stations distributed throughout the Cygnus cargo volume tracked smoke particulate transport, CO₂ accumulation, and cabin pressure rise.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 200 mm long × 400 mm wide structured cast PMMA slab (10 mm base thickness with ten 3 mm-high ribs of 1–10 mm width on both sides; 16 mm total thickness)

Source-supported test conditions for SAFFIRE-V Sample V-4 (structured PMMA in opposed flow): NTRS 20210017838 (Eigenbrod et al., ICES-2021-218, Abstract & Slide 3) reports inflow conditions of 26.9 vol% O₂, 761 hPa (76.1 kPa), 20 cm/s opposed flow for 360 s followed by 5 cm/s for 300 s (660 s total forced-flow duration), and opposed flame spread rate up to 0.88 mm/s along the 1 mm wide rib. Companion overview paper NTRS 20210011521 (Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Table 1, p. 3) lists SAFFIRE-V Sample V-4 at 25.7 mol% O₂ and 72.6 kPa, Sample V-2 (Cotton Jersey, 41 × 50 cm, concurrent) at 26.2 mol% O₂ and 70.7 kPa, and Sample V-3 (1-sided flat 5 mm PMMA, 40 × 18 cm, concurrent) at 25.4 mol% O₂ and 71.3 kPa. Note: The 34% O₂ / 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) atmosphere previously attached to this record was a NASA pre-flight exploration planning boundary (NTRS 20170000230, p. 7), NOT an actual SAFFIRE-V flight test condition; previously claimed 2.65 ± 0.22 mm/s spread rate, 420 s duration, and 15.2% LOI were contradicted/unverified and removed.

records.originalValue: Despite reduced total pressure (56.5 kPa), 34% O₂ enrichment creates a highly reactive fire environment with rapid ignition, intense radiative heating, and measurable far-field smoke and CO₂ dispersion across the spacecraft cabin.
records.activeValue: In SAFFIRE-V Sample V-4 (200 × 400 mm structured PMMA with 3 mm-high ribs of 1–10 mm width, tested at 26.9 vol% O₂ / 761 hPa [76.1 kPa] in NTRS 20210017838; 25.7 mol% O₂ / 72.6 kPa in NTRS 20210011521 Table 1), initial ignition after preheating produced a rapid (<100 ms) stratified-vapor deflagration, followed by opposed-flow flame spread along the ribs at up to 0.88 mm/s on the 1 mm rib (decreasing with rib width), oxygen-shadowing extinction of downstream flames, and rapid extinction when airflow was shut off after 300 s of 5 cm/s convective cooling (NTRS 20210017838 Abstract & Slides 3, 11; NTRS 20210011521 pp. 3–11).

records.originalValue: Exploration atmospheres with ~34% O₂ at ~56.5 kPa represent a substantially higher flammability and thermal hazard than 21% O₂ ISS air, requiring dedicated material screening and post-fire scrubbing evaluation.
records.activeValue: Thin surface ribs and edges on an otherwise thick (10 mm base) PMMA component act as thermally thin flame-spread pathways in microgravity opposed flow, and flow perturbations or preheating in low-flow zones can create stratified fuel-vapor mixtures that ignite via rapid deflagration. Conversely, stepping airflow down to 5 cm/s to cool the solid before fan shutoff prevented the delayed vapor-jet reignition observed when flow was cut abruptly in SAFFIRE-IV.

originalValue: Thin SIBAL strips (2.2 cm width) were burned in the MSG 7.6 cm × 7.6 cm duct across vitiated nitrogen/oxygen mixtures (16–21% O₂) and low flow velocities (1–35 cm/s).
Flame spread rate decreased monotonically with falling airflow until hitting a low-velocity radiative quenching limit.
Minimum Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) in microgravity forced flow dropped near 16.5% O₂, lower than Earth normal-gravity upward extinction thresholds under gentle forced flow.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 2.2 cm and 1.2 cm wide × 10 cm exposed length flat strips (0.32 mm thickness, 18.2 mg/cm² area density) in 7.6 cm × 7.6 cm × 17 cm flow duct

Source-supported baseline test conditions from NTRS 20150008962 (Zhao, T'ien, Ferkul, Olson, 2015, Section 2–3, pp. 2–4, Figure 2 & Appendix Test GMT96-T7, p. 9; also NASA/TM-20210011385 Section 7.0, pp. 93–101): 2.2 cm × 10 cm SIBAL strip at 10 cm/s concurrent flow, 21% O₂, 1 atm (101.3 kPa), reaching a limiting constant length at ~19 s with steady spread for ~9 s and total burn duration of ~40 s (and >60 s at 5 cm/s in Test GMT96-T8, Fig. 3). Across 27 BASS-II tests (16.4–21.0% O₂, 1–53 cm/s), low-speed quenching velocities were measured between 1 and 5 cm/s (e.g., quenching at 2.2 cm/s in 18.7% O₂ in Test GMT45-T4, Figs. 5–6). Because steady spread rates are plotted graphically in Figure 4 (p. 5) without a numeric table for the previously claimed 1.45 ± 0.11 mm/s and 16.2 ± 0.4% LOI, those unverified point values remain null.

records.originalValue: In microgravity low-speed forced flow (1–15 cm/s), thin cellulosic fabric exhibits both a low-flow radiative quenching boundary (near 1–3 cm/s) and a lower Limiting Oxygen Index (~16.5% O₂) than standard Earth natural-convection benchmarks.
records.activeValue: Across 27 BASS-II and 4 BASS concurrent-flow tests on 1.2 cm and 2.2 cm wide × 10 cm long SIBAL fabric strips in the ISS MSG duct (16.4–21% O₂, 1 atm, 1–53 cm/s), flames at 5–10 cm/s (21% O₂) reached steady limiting lengths and spread rates (~40 s total burn at 10 cm/s; >60 s at 5 cm/s), while stepping flow velocity down revealed a radiative/conductive low-speed quenching boundary between 1 and 5 cm/s where flames shrank into dim blue circular shapes before extinguishing (NTRS 20150008962 pp. 1–9; NTRS 20210011385 Section 7.0 pp. 93–101).

records.originalValue: Quiescent or zero-flow regions promote radiative self-extinguishment, whereas gentle cabin ventilation (5–15 cm/s) stabilizes flame spread even in slightly oxygen-vitiated atmospheres.
records.activeValue: Microgravity eliminates buoyant natural convection (which is ~20–30 cm/s in 1g), exposing a low-velocity regime (5–15 cm/s) where thin fabrics sustain steady concurrent spread, bounded below by radiative/conductive quenching at 1–5 cm/s (with higher quenching speeds required at lower O₂ concentrations).

originalValue: Cylindrical cast PMMA rods and flat PMMA samples were ignited in microgravity inside the ISS MSG duct.
Under opposed and concurrent flows between 1.5 and 25 cm/s, steady spread over PMMA rods proceeded at ~0.42 mm/s near 21% O₂ and 10 cm/s.
Extinction occurred when oxygen fell below ~17.5% O₂ or when forced flow dropped below radiative quenching thresholds.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 6.35 mm, 9.52 mm, and 12.7 mm diameter (radii 0.318, 0.476, and 0.635 cm) × 5.9 cm initial length cylindrical rods with hemispherical stagnation tips

Source-supported values from NASA/TM-20210011385 (NTRS 20210011385, Section 6.1, Olson, pp. 64–76): Across tests spanning 13.6–22.2% O₂ and 0–55 cm/s flow on 5.9 cm long PMMA rods (radii 0.318, 0.476, 0.635 cm), the empirical U-shaped flammability boundary (Eq. 6.1, Figs. 6.9–6.10, pp. 75–76) reaches a minimum oxygen concentration of 13.5% O₂ at stretch rate a = 8–12 s⁻¹ (1.9% O₂ lower than the 15.4% O₂ normal-gravity upward limit). In the lowest-O₂ quenching test (r = 0.476 cm rod, initial 14.8% O₂, final 13.6% O₂, flow stepped down to 1.5 cm/s, Figs. 6.4–6.6, pp. 69–72), the rod tip reached a steady-state regression velocity Vr = 0.0385 mm/s and oscillated at 1.1 Hz before quenching. Because this record spans a multi-test flammability boundary with quench tests lasting up to 28 min (p. 69), single-point ambient conditions and burn duration are left null; previously claimed 100 mm length, 0.18 ± 0.03 mm/s spread rate, 17.4% LOI, and 95 s duration were contradicted/unverified and removed.
records.explanation: Earlier pre-audit claims (100 mm rod length, 0.18 mm/s spread rate, 17.4% O₂ LOI, 95 s burn duration) were contradicted by NASA/TM-20210011385 Section 6.1, which reports initial rod length Lo = 5.9 cm (p. 64), three radii (0.318, 0.476, 0.635 cm, p. 67), steady rod tip regression rate Vr = 0.0385 mm/s at 13.6% O₂ quenching (p. 69), and a U-shaped flammability boundary minimum of 13.5% O₂ at stretch rate a = 8–12 s⁻¹ vs. 15.4% O₂ in 1g upward burning (pp. 75–76). Updated active record.
records.reviewerNotes: Verified against NASA/TM-20210011385 Section 6.1 (pp. 64–76).

records.originalValue: Cast PMMA exhibits slower flame spread (~0.42 mm/s) and a slightly higher LOI (~17.5% O₂) than thin SIBAL fabric in microgravity low-speed flows, with extinction governed by surface radiative heat losses at very low velocities.
records.activeValue: In BASS-II axial stagnation-flow tests on cast PMMA rods (radii 0.318–0.635 cm, initial length 5.9 cm) across 13.6–22.2% O₂ and 0–55 cm/s flow, sustained ignition required ≥14.5% O₂ (with ignition delays up to 230 s near the limit), but pre-warmed burning rods survived down to 13.6% O₂ (with steady rod tip regression of 0.0385 mm/s and 1.1 Hz flame oscillations prior to radiative quenching), defining a U-shaped flammability boundary with a minimum of 13.5% O₂ at low stretch rates (8–12 s⁻¹) compared to 15.4% O₂ in 1g upward screening (NTRS 20210011385 Section 6.1, pp. 64–76).

records.originalValue: Reducing forced ventilation below critical quenching speeds suppresses thick polymer flames in microgravity, whereas persistent 10–15 cm/s ventilation sustains slow but steady burning.
records.activeValue: PMMA rods in microgravity remain flammable in a low-velocity 'Goldilocks' ventilation zone (~1–5 cm/s) down to 13.5% O₂—1.9% O₂ lower than normal-gravity upward screening (15.4% O₂)—and require up to 230 s to ignite near the limit, showing that NASA-STD-6001 Test 1's 25 s normal-gravity ignition protocol is non-conservative for preheated thick polymers in low-speed spacecraft ventilation.

originalValue: Large isolated n-heptane droplets (2.5–4.5 mm initial diameter) formed spherical diffusion flames in quiescent microgravity inside the ISS CIR.
Unlike small droplets that burn out completely, larger heptane droplets experienced radiative extinction of the hot visible flame while droplet fuel remained.
Following visible hot-flame extinction, n-heptane droplets continued vaporizing under non-visible low-temperature cool-flame combustion producing partial oxidation products.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 2–5 mm initial diameter free-floating and 80-µm fiber-supported spherical droplets (Test FLEX-008: 2.95 mm ± 0.05 mm initial diameter free-floating n-heptane droplet)

Source-supported test point for FLEX-008 (identifier 30CAL06, April 10, 2009) from NASA/TP-2015-216046 (NTRS 20150023456, Table I p. 9 & Table IX p. 20): free-floating n-heptane droplet in ISS cabin air (0.21 O₂ mole fraction, 0.79 N₂, 762.4 mmHg = 101.6 kPa), actual initial diameter D₀ = 2.95 mm (±50 µm [±0.05 mm] HiBMs droplet diameter uncertainty per Section 3.1.2, p. 8), average burning-rate constant K = 0.79 mm²/s, and burn time 14.8 s (companion cabin-air test FLEX-007 with D₀ = 1.87 mm had K = 0.67 mm²/s and burn time 5.3 s). Across the 284-test campaign (0.70–3.05 atm), N₂-diluted heptane tests (Table V, p. 12) were conducted down to 13.4% O₂. Linear flame spread rate (mm/s) is not applicable to spherical droplet regression (mm²/s). Previously claimed 6.8 s burn duration and 13.8 ± 0.5% LOI were contradicted/unverified in NASA/TP-2015-216046 and removed.

records.originalValue: Discovered dual-stage combustion in microgravity liquid heptane droplets: visible flames extinguish radiatively below ~15–21% O₂ depending on diluent, yet low-temperature cool flames persist invisibly, generating aldehydes and CO.
records.activeValue: In NASA/TP-2015-216046 (archiving the first 284 FLEX tests on ISS), free-floating n-heptane and methanol droplets (2–5 mm initial diameter) burned with spherical symmetry in quiescent microgravity across 0.70–3.05 atm, exhibiting radiative extinction at larger droplet diameters under high dilution, diffusive extinction at smaller diameters, and disruptive extinction; in cabin air (Test FLEX-008: 21% O₂, 762.4 mmHg [101.6 kPa]), a 2.95 mm n-heptane droplet burned for 14.8 s with an average d²-law burning-rate constant of K = 0.79 mm²/s (NTRS 20150023456, pp. 1, 8–12, 20).

records.originalValue: Absence of visible flame emission in quiescent microgravity does not guarantee complete chemical extinction; optical-only sensors may miss smoldering or cool-flame vapor oxidation.
records.activeValue: Spherical droplet combustion in quiescent microgravity is governed by diffusive and radiative heat/mass transfer rather than buoyant convection, with large droplets susceptible to radiative extinction and visible soot shells (in n-heptane) residing inside the outer OH* chemiluminescence flame zone (where visible flame diameters are ~3/4 of LLUV OH* diameters, Section 4.2 p. 15).

originalValue: Used a 50 mm diameter flat porous stainless-steel burner fed with gaseous ethylene or methane diluted with nitrogen to emulate heats of gasification of solid polymers and textiles.
Controlled fuel mass flux and measured radiative heat feedback and surface temperature across reduced pressures and varying oxygen levels.
Mapped steady burning vs extinction limits independent of transient solid-fuel pyrolysis geometry.
activeValue: Sample geometry: 25 mm and 50 mm diameter circular porous gas-fueled burners with perforated outlet plates and heat-flux sensors

Investigation overview record backed by NTRS 20170009141 (Markan, Quintiere, Sunderland, de Ris, Stocker, 2017, pp. 1–6) and NTRS 20160010073 (Markan et al., 2015, Slides 1–10): ~53 microgravity drop tests (5.18 s free fall) were conducted across 25 mm and 50 mm burner diameters, 21–30% O₂ (0.21–0.30 mole fraction), 0.5–1.0 atm (50.7–101.3 kPa), and 3.5–12.7 g/m²s fuel flux to emulate condensed fuels with heats of gasification L = 0.4–4 kJ/g. In Test 92 (ethylene, 30% O₂, 0.7 atm, NTRS 20160010073 Slide 5), net surface heat flux reached ~3 kW/m² on the 25 mm burner vs. ~7 kW/m² on the 50 mm burner. Single-point conditions and measurements remain null on this overview record; previously cited NTRS 20205008253 returned HTTP 404 and was replaced with verified NTRS 20170009141 and NTRS 20160010073.

records.originalValue: Investigation overview: BRE provides fundamental flammability boundary maps across 15–35% O₂ and 50–101.3 kPa by matching thermal feedback and gasification parameters of real spacecraft materials.
records.activeValue: Microgravity Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) tests using 25 mm and 50 mm circular gas burners (methane and ethylene across 21–30% O₂ and 0.5–1.0 atm in quiescent microgravity) produced hemispherical flames whose surface heat flux approached quasi-steady state within ~5 s (while flame height reached only ~37% of steady state in 5 s, motivating long-duration ISS tests), and demonstrated higher net surface heat flux on the 50 mm burner (~7 kW/m² vs. ~3 kW/m² at 30% O₂, 0.7 atm) due to increased gas-phase radiation from the larger flame volume (NTRS 20170009141 pp. 1–6; NTRS 20160010073 Slides 3–6).

records.activeValue: Matching four condensed-fuel properties (heat of combustion, heat of gasification in 0.4–4 kJ/g, surface temperature, and smoke point) with a controlled gas burner allows isolation of steady mass-transfer (B-number) and gas-radiation scaling effects without solid-phase melting Distortion, while proving that >5 s ISS test durations are required for thermal and flame-height equilibrium.

originalValue: Ongoing ISS CIR experimental module designed to measure ignition delay, thermally-assisted flame spread, and suppression limits on cylindrical PMMA samples.
Incorporates controlled external radiant heat flux, oxygen concentration, total pressure, and forced flow speed to bridge ISS and exploration cabin atmospheres.
activeValue: Sample geometry: Cylindrical cast PMMA rods (12.7 mm diameter × 150–154 mm length) centered in a 70 mm ID quartz flow tube with three equispaced halogen radiant heaters (up to 40 kW/m²) and downstream Kanthal wire pilot

Investigation overview record backed by NTRS 20200000361 (Ferkul et al., 2019, Slides 3–5, 11–16) and NTRS 20150023467 (Fernandez-Pello, 2013, pp. 1–13): MIST apparatus tests 12.7 mm diameter × 154 mm length cast PMMA rods (22 rod samples of 15 cm nominal length allocated in SoFIE CIR insert, NTRS 20200000361 Slide 11) under external radiant flux up to 40 kW/m², 14–30% O₂, and 10–100 cm/s flow. Direct numerical simulations in NTRS 20150023467 (Section Modeling Task, pp. 8–10, Figs. 12–13) at 100 kPa, 21% O₂, 40 cm/s (0.4 m/s) flow, and 16 kW/m² radiant flux predicted piloted ignition at 596 s in 0g vs. 774 s in 1g. Single-point flight measurements remain null on this overview record; previously cited NTRS 20220014842 was an unrelated aircraft human-autonomy paper and was replaced with verified NTRS 20200000361 and NTRS 20150023467.

records.originalValue: Investigation overview: SoFIE-MIST targets thermally-assisted solid-fuel ignition and suppression limits under exploration-relevant oxygen/pressure combinations aboard the ISS.
records.activeValue: The SoFIE-MIST investigation and apparatus (12.7 mm × 150–154 mm cast PMMA rods irradiated by three halogen heaters up to 40 kW/m² across 14–30% O₂ and 10–100 cm/s flow) demonstrated an exponential decay in ignition delay time with increasing incident radiant heat flux, an approximately constant critical mass loss rate at ignition across heat fluxes, statistically significant differences between virgin and re-ignited PMMA samples, and earlier predicted piloted ignition in microgravity than normal gravity (596 s in 0g vs. 774 s in 1g at 16 kW/m², 21% O₂, 100 kPa, 40 cm/s in FDS-DNS modeling) due to absence of buoyant Rayleigh-Taylor cooling instabilities (NTRS 20200000361 Slides 4, 11; NTRS 20150023467 pp. 2–10).

records.activeValue: External radiant heat flux from adjacent overheated equipment or fire plumes lowers ignition delay times in microgravity compared to 1g because the absence of buoyant convective cooling allows steeper thermal and pyrolyzate boundary layers to accumulate near the downstream pilot.

records.originalValue: Conducted realistic spacecraft combustion and far-field smoke/gas diagnostics under an exploration-class reduced-pressure, elevated-oxygen atmosphere (56.5 kPa, 34% O₂) after Cygnus unberthing.
records.activeValue: Conducted large-scale spacecraft fire growth, extinction, and far-field smoke/gas transport experiments inside Cygnus (NG-14, January 2021) at reduced pressure and elevated oxygen (reported as 25.4–26.2 mol% O₂ and 70.7–72.6 kPa across Samples V-2, V-3, and V-4 in NTRS 20210011521 Table 1, and 26.9 vol% O₂ at 761 hPa [76.1 kPa] for structured PMMA Sample V-4 in NTRS 20210017838). Note: 34% O₂ / 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) is a NASA exploration atmosphere planning reference (NTRS 20170000230), not an established SAFFIRE-V flight test condition.
records.explanation: Original summary claimed SAFFIRE-V ran at '56.5 kPa, 34% O₂'. Primary post-flight SAFFIRE-V papers contradict this: NTRS 20210011521 Table 1 (p. 3) reports 25.4–26.2 mol% O₂ and 70.7–72.6 kPa across Samples V-2, V-3, and V-4, and NTRS 20210017838 (Abstract & Slide 3) reports 26.9 vol% O₂ and 761 hPa (76.1 kPa) for structured PMMA Sample V-4. The 34% O₂ / 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia) setting was a pre-flight planning boundary (NTRS 20170000230, p. 7). Updated active summary.

originalValue.measurementNotes: Source-supported results from NTRS 20180005168 Table 1 (Slides 30–31): In Sample II-7 (20 cm/s concurrent flow, ~22.1% O₂, 80 W igniter for 9.2 s), the 5 cm PMMA starter burned for 140 s (5 cm burn length), but the adjacent 24 cm Nomex fabric (0.37 mm thick) exhibited 0 cm burn length and no sustained flame spread (0.0 mm/s). Similarly, all four Silicone strips (II-1 to II-4, thicknesses 0.27–1.03 mm at 20 cm/s, ~22.1% O₂) exhibited 'Insignificant' burn duration and ~0 cm microgravity burn length (whereas 1g comparison strips burned completely or 7.6 cm for II-1, II-2, II-4). Previously claimed 0.8 mm thickness, 3.2 s burn duration, and 22.5% MOC were contradicted/unverified and removed.

activeValue.measurementNotes: NTRS 20180005168, Table 1: Nomex did not sustain propagation and silicone samples had insignificant burn duration. No numerical propagation rate or uncertainty is asserted by this record.

originalValue.measurementNotes: Source-supported test conditions for SAFFIRE-V Sample V-4 (structured PMMA in opposed flow): NTRS 20210017838 (Eigenbrod et al., ICES-2021-218, Abstract & Slide 3) reports inflow conditions of 26.9 vol% O₂, 761 hPa (76.1 kPa), 20 cm/s opposed flow for 360 s followed by 5 cm/s for 300 s (660 s total forced-flow duration), and opposed flame spread rate up to 0.88 mm/s along the 1 mm wide rib. Companion overview paper NTRS 20210011521 (Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Table 1, p. 3) lists SAFFIRE-V Sample V-4 at 25.7 mol% O₂ and 72.6 kPa, Sample V-2 (Cotton Jersey, 41 × 50 cm, concurrent) at 26.2 mol% O₂ and 70.7 kPa, and Sample V-3 (1-sided flat 5 mm PMMA, 40 × 18 cm, concurrent) at 25.4 mol% O₂ and 71.3 kPa. originalValue.measurementNotes: Source-supported values from NASA/TM-20210011385 (NTRS 20210011385, Section 6.1, Olson, pp. 64–76): Across tests spanning 13.6–22.2% O₂ and 0–55 cm/s flow on 5.9 cm long PMMA rods (radii 0.318, 0.476, 0.635 cm), the empirical U-shaped flammability boundary (Eq. 6.1, Figs. 6.9–6.10, pp. 75–76) reaches a minimum oxygen concentration of 13.5% O₂ at stretch rate a = 8–12 s⁻¹ (1.9% O₂ lower than the 15.4% O₂ normal-gravity upward limit). In the lowest-O₂ quenching test (r = 0.476 cm rod, initial 14.8% O₂, final 13.6% O₂, flow stepped down to 1.5 cm/s, Figs. 6.4–6.6, pp. 69–72), the rod tip reached a steady-state regression velocity Vr = 0.0385 mm/s and oscillated at 1.1 Hz before quenching. Because this record spans a multi-test flammability boundary with quench tests lasting up to 28 min (p. 69), single-point ambient conditions and burn duration are left null; previously claimed 100 mm length, 0.18 ± 0.03 mm/s spread rate, 17.4% LOI, and 95 s duration were contradicted/unverified and removed.

remediation.originalValue: Across 27 BASS-II and 4 BASS concurrent-flow tests on 1.2 cm and 2.2 cm wide × 10 cm long SIBAL fabric strips in the ISS MSG duct (16.4–21% O₂, 1 atm, 1–53 cm/s), flames at 5–10 cm/s (21% O₂) reached steady limiting lengths and spread rates (~40 s total burn at 10 cm/s; >60 s at 5 cm/s), while stepping flow velocity down revealed a radiative/conductive low-speed quenching boundary between 1 and 5 cm/s where flames shrank into dim blue circular shapes before extinguishing (NTRS 20150008962 pp. 1–9; NTRS 20210011385 Section 7.0 pp. 93–101).
remediation.activeValue: BASS-II SIBAL tests showed limiting flame lengths and low-speed quenching in a small ISS duct. This record uses the documented GMT96-T7 baseline conditions (21% oxygen, 101.3 kPa, 10 cm/s). No numerical spread-rate value is extracted from the plotted curve.

originalValue.measurementNotes: Source-supported values from NASA/TM-20210011385 (NTRS 20210011385, Section 6.1, Olson, pp. 64–76): Across tests spanning 13.6–22.2% O₂ and 0–55 cm/s flow on 5.9 cm long PMMA rods (radii 0.318, 0.476, 0.635 cm), the empirical U-shaped flammability boundary (Eq. 6.1, Figs. 6.9–6.10, pp. 75–76) reaches a minimum oxygen concentration of 13.5% O₂ at stretch rate a = 8–12 s⁻¹ (1.9% O₂ lower than the 15.4% O₂ normal-gravity upward limit). In the lowest-O₂ quenching test (r = 0.476 cm rod, initial 14.8% O₂, final 13.6% O₂, flow stepped down to 1.5 cm/s, Figs. 6.4–6.6, pp. 69–72), the rod tip reached a steady-state regression velocity Vr = 0.0385 mm/s and oscillated at 1.1 Hz before quenching. Because this record spans a multi-test flammability boundary with quench tests lasting up to 28 min (p. 69), single-point ambient conditions and burn duration are left null; previously claimed 100 mm length, 0.18 ± 0.03 mm/s spread rate, 17.4% LOI, and 95 s duration were contradicted/unverified and removed.

remediation.originalValue: In BASS-II axial stagnation-flow tests on cast PMMA rods (radii 0.318–0.635 cm, initial length 5.9 cm) across 13.6–22.2% O₂ and 0–55 cm/s flow, sustained ignition required ≥14.5% O₂ (with ignition delays up to 230 s near the limit), but pre-warmed burning rods survived down to 13.6% O₂ (with steady rod tip regression of 0.0385 mm/s and 1.1 Hz flame oscillations prior to radiative quenching), defining a U-shaped flammability boundary with a minimum of 13.5% O₂ at low stretch rates (8–12 s⁻¹) compared to 15.4% O₂ in 1g upward screening (NTRS 20210011385 Section 6.1, pp. 64–76).
remediation.activeValue: BASS-II PMMA rods exhibited a steady rod-tip regression velocity of 0.0385 mm/s in the quenching test described on page 69. Separately, the fitted multi-test flammability boundary reached a minimum oxygen concentration of 13.5%. These are distinct quantities and scopes; 13.5% is not the setpoint for the regression measurement or a safe cabin setting.

remediation.originalValue: Microgravity Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) tests using 25 mm and 50 mm circular gas burners (methane and ethylene across 21–30% O₂ and 0.5–1.0 atm in quiescent microgravity) produced hemispherical flames whose surface heat flux approached quasi-steady state within ~5 s (while flame height reached only ~37% of steady state in 5 s, motivating long-duration ISS tests), and demonstrated higher net surface heat flux on the 50 mm burner (~7 kW/m² vs. ~3 kW/m² at 30% O₂, 0.7 atm) due to increased gas-phase radiation from the larger flame volume (NTRS 20170009141 pp. 1–6; NTRS 20160010073 Slides 3–6).
remediation.activeValue: The cited BRE study used circular gas burners to emulate condensed-fuel burning during short-duration microgravity drop tests. It discusses transient flame and surface-heat-flux behavior. These ground-facility results are not a single ISS flight measurement.

remediation.activeValue: The SoFIE-MIST sources describe an apparatus and research program for ignition of radiantly heated PMMA rods. remediation.old: Thin surface ribs and edges on an otherwise thick (10 mm base) PMMA component act as thermally thin flame-spread pathways in microgravity opposed flow, and flow perturbations or preheating in low-flow zones can create stratified fuel-vapor mixtures that ignite via rapid deflagration. Conversely, stepping airflow down to 5 cm/s to cool the solid before fan shutoff prevented the delayed vapor-jet reignition observed when flow was cut abruptly in SAFFIRE-IV.
remediation.new: Research interpretation: Separate the rib-spread maximum, changing airflow protocol, and differing published atmosphere reports. Do not infer an operational fan-shutdown procedure from this record.

remediation.new: Research interpretation: The low-flow behavior is relevant to small-duct research. The plotted campaign results cannot supply a missing scalar spread rate for an arbitrary cabin setting.

remediation.new: Research interpretation: Keep a multi-test flammability boundary separate from a single rod-regression observation. Neither quantity is a safe-oxygen limit for a spacecraft.

remediation.old: Spherical droplet combustion in quiescent microgravity is governed by diffusive and radiative heat/mass transfer rather than buoyant convection, with large droplets susceptible to radiative extinction and visible soot shells (in n-heptane) residing inside the outer OH* chemiluminescence flame zone (where visible flame diameters are ~3/4 of LLUV OH* diameters, Section 4.2 p. 15).
remediation.new: Research interpretation: Droplet burn duration is a different physical quantity from solid-material flame spread. FLEX-008 ended in droplet disruption; its duration is not an extinction threshold.

remediation.old: Matching four condensed-fuel properties (heat of combustion, heat of gasification in 0.4–4 kJ/g, surface temperature, and smoke point) with a controlled gas burner allows isolation of steady mass-transfer (B-number) and gas-radiation scaling effects without solid-phase melting Distortion, while proving that >5 s ISS test durations are required for thermal and flame-height equilibrium.
remediation.new: Research interpretation: This ground study informs burner-emulation research. It does not establish a measured ISS operating point or a validated condensed-material prediction.
